    Example 4.2: injections of countable ordinals into ℕ #

    For a countable ordinal i, let S_i be the set of injections [0, i) ↪ ℕ whose image misses infinitely many numbers, with restriction as transition maps (Bergman, Wofsey). Restriction is surjective: enumerate the missed numbers, send the countably many new points injectively to the even positions of this enumeration, and the odd positions stay missed. A compatible family would give an injection ω₁ ↪ ℕ, so lim S = ∅, while S_0 is a single point. By Lemma 4.1 and Theorem B, C(k^(S)) has no triangulated embedding.
